issues.description: Lecture class field identifiers: the solution/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Lecture.java file declares private fields using snake_case names (lecture_name, number_of_inscribed_students, number_of_guest_students, number_of_lecturers, number_of_tutors) but the constructor, getters, setters and other methods in the same solution file refer to camelCase identifiers (lectureName, numberOfInscribedStudents, numberOfGuestStudents, numberOfLecturers, numberOfTutors). The problem statement UML and the template expect camelCase names. This mismatch causes compilation errors (undefined symbol errors) and prevents students from compiling and running the provided solution, and it contradicts the UML and template expectations.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the field names in the solution Lecture.java consistent with the constructor and methods and with the UML/template. Rename the snake_case fields to camelCase: private String lectureName; private int numberOfInscribedStudents; private int numberOfGuestStudents; private int numberOfLecturers; private int numberOfTutors; Alternatively (less preferred), update all constructor, getter, setter and method references to use the snake_case names. Prefer using camelCase to match the UML, template, and Java conventions.

issues.description: The exercise identifies attributes named with camelCase in the problem/UML: lectureName, numberOfInscribedStudents, numberOfGuestStudents, numberOfLecturers, numberOfTutors. In the solution implementation the private fields are declared with snake_case identifiers (lecture_name, number_of_inscribed_students, number_of_guest_students, number_of_lecturers, number_of_tutors) while the constructor and public methods refer to camelCase identifiers (lectureName, numberOfInscribedStudents, numberOfGuestStudents, numberOfLecturers, numberOfTutors). The template file contains only TODOs for these attributes and does not declare names. This mismatch means students cannot reliably map the UML names to the actual fields in the provided solution, and the solution as written is inconsistent and will not compile because methods reference names that do not exist. Students will be confused about which identifiers are canonical and may waste time renaming or debugging.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the attribute identifiers consistent with the UML/problem statement and across the implementation. Rename the private fields in the solution to camelCase to match the UML: private String lectureName; private int numberOfInscribedStudents; private int numberOfGuestStudents; private int numberOfLecturers; private int numberOfTutors; and update all usages accordingly (constructor assignments, getters, setters, and methods). Alternatively, change the constructor parameters and all method references to use the snake_case names — but prefer adopting the camelCase names from the UML/problem statement so students can directly map requirements to code.
